articles.title: How Agile Teams Turn Weaknesses Into Delivery Superpowers
articles.excerpt: The Weakness Paradox in Software Delivery "What is your biggest weakness?" It is the question leaders hate answering during job interviews. Yet, the highest-performing Agile teams ask a variation of t…
articles.body: The Weakness Paradox in Software Delivery "What is your biggest weakness?" It is the question leaders hate answering during job interviews. Yet, the highest-performing Agile teams ask a variation of this question every single Sprint to unlock hidden velocity and prevent catastrophic deployment failures. For decades, traditional corporate management trained us to hide our flaws. We were taught to project invincibility. Never let them see you sweat. In complex software delivery, however, faking it is a massive liability. Pretending you have all the answers is the fastest way to ship the wrong product, and ship it late. The illusion of perfection creates a fragile environment where mistakes are hidden until they blow up in production.
articles.author: Alireza Razmara

While growth is good, if that surge is due to bots, malicious actors, or even just an overly enthusiastic client, it can quickly turn into a nightmare. Without proper controls, your backend services can become overwhelmed, leading to: Performance Degradation: Slow response times, timeouts, and complete service unavailability, frustrating legitimate users. Exorbitant Cloud Bills: Unchecked requests translate directly to higher compute, database, and bandwidth costs, leading to unexpected and alarming infrastructure expenses.

articles.body: Disclosure: I'm Ben, and I built the Apify tool I mention near the end. It charges per result. The DIY part below works with free stuff only. If you sell to new UK companies, or you're an accountant looking for first-year clients, the official register is the right place to start. You don't need a Companies House API key for a basic leads list. Companies House publishes a monthly snapshot of live companies, for free, under the Open Government Licence v3.0. The file is called the Free Company Data Product . It's a snapshot of companies on the register, compiled to the end of the previous month and usually published within 5 working days of month end. It's not a same-day feed. A company incorporated this week shows up in the next snapshot.

articles.title: Designing a Cost-Per-Use Tracker for Android: Calculations, State and Data Integrity
articles.excerpt: Most personal finance applications focus on transactions. You buy something, record the amount, assign a category, and move on. But what if the interesting part of a purchase begins after the transact…
articles.body: Most personal finance applications focus on transactions. You buy something, record the amount, assign a category, and move on. But what if the interesting part of a purchase begins after the transaction? Consider a pair of shoes, a laptop, or a power tool. The purchase price is fixed, but its practical value changes as the item is used, repaired, returned, or eventually sold. At TSI Dev Studio, this question influenced the development of HEZX , our local-first Android purchase and cost-per-use tracker. HEZX helps users follow an item from its return window through years of recorded usage and ownership history. Building a useful product around that concept raises several interesting software design questions.

articles.body: CVE-2025-42884 remediation without overstating the evidence Known exploitation is enough to raise priority, but it is not a substitute for evidence about this vulnerability. CVE-2025-42884 has a KEV listing, a vendor note, a clear affected component range, and a public description of JNDI lookup injection. It does not have a public exploit chain in the reviewed sources. A strong remediation record keeps both sides visible. Vulnerability overview SAP Security Note 3660969 addresses CVE-2025-42884 in SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal. The bulletin lists EP-BASIS 7.50 and EP-RUNTIME 7.50, CVSS 3.1 6.5, and CWE-943. CISA added the issue to KEV on November 20, 2026 with a November 23 due date.

articles.title: Retrieval Quality and Latency Fallbacks Explained — Recruiting Candidate Search
articles.excerpt: Short answer: give recruiting candidate search a strict latency budget, spend it on the highest-quality retrieval that can still finish, and return an explicit degraded result rather than letting hidd…
articles.body: Short answer: give recruiting candidate search a strict latency budget, spend it on the highest-quality retrieval that can still finish, and return an explicit degraded result rather than letting hidden fallbacks consume the whole request. A logistics page changes and the on-call alert says only "content changed." There is no shipment identifier, no changed sentence, and no clue whether somebody should act. The page fired, but the useful signal arrived too late: retrieval did not extract enough evidence before the alert deadline. Candidate search has the same operational tension. A recruiter needs relevant profiles with supporting text, yet an exhaustive rescue path that stalls the interaction is not a rescue. I've been paged by missed jobs and duplicate deliveries.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of lightwhile observing Jupiter and its moon volcanic moon Io. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule.

articles.body: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit .

articles.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
articles.excerpt: The BepiColombo spacecraft will finally arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.
articles.body: Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.

articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast.
articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026.
